newsitem.title: FRANCE: Council must coordinate policies post-EMU -Trichet.
newsitem.headline: Council must coordinate policies post-EMU -Trichet.

text.p: European central banks agree European Union governments must coordinate their policies closely once a single currency is launched in 1999, Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet said on Tuesday.

"There is a consensus among all the governors of independent central banks in Europe that it is very important that the council should be able to coordinate closely enough so that budgetary and general economic policies function as well as possible," Trichet said at an annual news conference.
There would have to be "a very intense cooperation between the governments of the countries inside the euro zone," he said.

Such co-operation in no way threatened the independence of the future European Central Bank (ECB), any more than the independence of the U.S. Federal Reserve or of the Bank of France was threatened by the existence of governments in their countries running economic policies, Trichet said.
The idea of questioning the independence of the ECB, which was guaranteed by the Maastricht treaty, was "not in the minds of anyone whatsoever in Paris", he said.

He had been asked his views on comments on Saturday by President Jacques Chirac that countries in the euro zone should hold summits and ministerial meetings to coordinate economic policies after the launch of the single European currency and act as a counterbalance to the power of the central bank.
